text: # APIs An API is an interface that allows software components to communicate. HTTP APIs commonly use methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. An API endpoint identifies a resource or operation. A REST-style API commonly represents resources using URLs and HTTP methods.

# Asynchronous JavaScript JavaScript supports asynchronous programming with callbacks, promises, and async/await. A Promise represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation. The async keyword defines an asynchronous function. The await keyword pauses execution of an async function until a Promise settles.

# Error Handling Backend applications should handle errors explicitly. Express applications can use error-handling middleware. An Express error handler has the signature: (err, req, res, next) Applications should return appropriate HTTP status codes and avoid exposing sensitive internal information.

# Express.js Express is a web framework for Node.js. It provides routing, middleware support, request and response handling, and utilities for building HTTP APIs. An Express application typically creates an app instance and registers middleware and routes. Example: const express = require("express"); const app = express(); app.get("/", (req, res) => { res.json({ message: "Hello" }); }); Middleware functions can access the request object, response object, and the next function.

# JavaScript JavaScript is a programming language commonly used for web development. Modern JavaScript supports modules, classes, promises, async and await, destructuring, and many other language features. JavaScript can run in browsers and server environments such as Node.js.

# Express Middleware Express middleware functions execute during the request-response lifecycle. Middleware receives req, res, and next. Middleware can inspect requests, modify request or response objects, terminate a request, or call next() to continue. Common middleware examples include logging, authentication, JSON parsing, validation, and error handling.

# MongoDB MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database. MongoDB stores records as BSON documents. Documents are organized into collections. Applications can communicate with MongoDB using drivers or libraries such as Mongoose. MongoDB is commonly used with Node.js applications.

# Node.js Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on the V8 JavaScript engine. It allows JavaScript to execute outside the browser. Node.js is commonly used for backend services, APIs, command-line tools, and event-driven applications. Node.js uses an event loop to coordinate asynchronous operations.

# REST APIs REST is an architectural style commonly used for web APIs. HTTP methods communicate the intended operation. GET commonly retrieves data. POST commonly creates data. PUT and PATCH commonly update data. DELETE commonly removes data. HTTP status codes communicate the result of an operation.

# Express Routing Routing determines how an Express application responds to requests for specific paths and HTTP methods. Express supports methods such as app.get(), app.post(), app.put(), app.patch(), and app.delete(). Routes can also be organized with express.Router().
